messages:
matt: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered INC-4321 — high error rate to cache provider (CacheForge Redis auth cluster). Token-cache miss rate +300%, rate-limiter falling back to DB and causing downstream latency spikes. Links: https://observability.redwood/graph/INC-4321, runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cacheforge-incident
incident-bot: Incident INC-4321 created and assigned to oncall (sara). Severity: P1. Auto-page: +1 oncall.
sara: I'm on it. Confirming blast radius: auth token cache miss -> every auth check hits userstore. Saw 5xx: connection reset by peer from cache nodes. Any recent deploys to cache stack?
matt: No deploys to cache infra in last 6h. Cloud provider (CacheForge) status shows partial degraded networking in eu-west-1. Their status: https://status.cacheforge.com/incidents/zz12
eli: Logs from proxy show repeated ECONNRESET to cache endpoint:```
2026-03-15T14:05:12Z auth-proxy ERROR connecting to cacheforge-eu1-01: read ECONNRESET
2026-03-15T14:05:14Z auth-proxy WARN cache miss fallback -> origin (DB)
```
rachel: On the rate-limiter side, we started emitting 429->500 cascades when cache returns errors. Frontend SLOs are seeing latency spikes ~600ms p95. Customer-visible errors: elevated login latencies and some 503s. CS flagged high priority tickets from two enterprise customers.
sara: First mitigation: enable degraded local bypass for rate-limiter so it doesn't backpressure upstream. Runbook suggests toggling env FLAG: RATE_LIMITER_CACHE_FALLBACK=local-short-ttl. Doing it now on canary:```
kubectl set env deploy/rate-limiter RATE_LIMITER_CACHE_FALLBACK=local-short-ttl -n prod-canary
```
matt: Canary looks good, no 5xx after toggling for canary. Rolling to prod in 2 batches. Also opening a support ticket with CacheForge asking for failover ETA and to promote a healthy node.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: oncall-reassign to jihoon in 30m for handoff.
eli: Additional short-term: increasing token TTL to reduce cache reads for auth checks:```
# temp change
REDWOOD_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL=90  # from 30s to 90s
```
This will slightly reduce security freshness but reduces DB load. Applying to prod-canary now.
sara: r=apply to prod after canary verification. Also enabling degraded-mode header to frontend so we can route non-critical clients to relaxed checks: `X-Auth-Degraded: 1`. Notify CS.
matt: CacheForge replied: "We're seeing a networking flap across a subset of nodes; failover is in progress, ETA ~15-25m. Recommend using read-replica endpoints as a workaround." They gave read-replica hostnames — switching traffic might require config push.
eli: I pushed a config to auth-proxy to prefer cacheforge-eu1-replica on read, command:```
kubectl patch cm auth-proxy-config -n prod -p '{"data":{"cache_host":"cacheforge-eu1-replica"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n prod
```
Rolling restart started. Monitoring.
rachel: Noting customer impact summary for postmortem: auth latencies up -> some login errors and elevated API latencies for webhook-backed integrations. No data loss. Affected region: eu-west-1 primarily. Initial estimate: 5-10% of active traffic experienced degraded auth within 14:05-14:40 UTC.
sara: Prod rollout complete. Post-change checks: 200 responses back to cache reads on replica, token-cache miss rate dropping. DB saturation reduced. Observability graphs: error-rate trending down.
matt: Confirmed CacheForge status updated: primary nodes recovering. They will run continuity checks.
sara: Escalation/communication: Rachel, please coordinate CS message with impact window and mitigations we applied. Use canned blurb from runbook and include guidance for customers hitting 503s to retry.
rachel: Will do. Draft: "We experienced an external cache provider outage impacting auth latency and some login attempts in eu-west-1 between 14:05-14:40 UTC. We applied degraded-mode routing, switched reads to replica, and increased token TTL to mitigate. No user data was lost. Contact support if ongoing issues."
matt: Next steps: follow CacheForge incident updates, revert TEMP config changes once stable (TTL and degraded header and fallback). Schedule postmortem with timeline and action items.
sara: Handoff notes for next oncall (@jihoon): summary + actions to monitor:
- Confirm CacheForge full recovery and node promotions
- Revert REDWOOD_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL to 30s when safe
- Remove RATE_LIMITER_CACHE_FALLBACK after 1h stable
- Run a synthetic login sweep in eu-west-1 and validate p95 latency < 300ms
- Coordinate with CS on any escalations

sara: Handoff -> @jihoon, taking over for next 8h. All context above + links: observability, runbook, support ticket id #CF-2026-312.
jihoon: Acknowledged. I'll monitor and coordinate reverts once CacheForge confirms. If we see any DB pressure climb again, I'll open emergency rollback.
incident-bot: Incident INC-4321 status: mitigated. Oncall: jihoon. Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-17 15:00 UTC.
matt: Great job team. :thumbsup:
sara: Closing this thread for active ops, keeping incident channel updated with any CacheForge updates.
